stem: What is an Azure virtual network?

choices.A: A billing agreement
choices.B: An isolated logical network with defined address space
choices.D: A managed file share

explanations.A: That is not a network construct.
explanations.B: A VNet organizes network connectivity in Azure.
explanations.C: That is authorization.

stem: What does a subnet do?

choices.A: Replicates blobs to another region
choices.D: Creates a separate Azure subscription

explanations.A: That is storage redundancy.
explanations.B: Network subdivision does not verify identity.
explanations.C: Subnets create address ranges within the network.
explanations.D: Subnetting does not create billing scopes.

stem: Why must subnet address ranges be planned?

choices.A: Subnets automatically fix all DNS names
choices.B: They must fit the VNet and avoid overlaps
choices.C: Each subnet must use the same complete prefix
choices.D: Private addresses guarantee all traffic is authorized

explanations.A: Address planning does not solve name resolution.
explanations.B: Valid ranges support predictable routing and allocation.
explanations.C: Overlapping ranges are invalid.
explanations.D: Addressing does not replace access control.

stem: What does VNet peering provide?

choices.A: A physical customer-owned circuit in every case
choices.B: Automatic replication of all application data
choices.D: Connectivity between virtual networks over Azure infrastructure

explanations.A: That describes a different connectivity approach.
explanations.C: Access policy remains necessary.

stem: A peers with B and B peers with C. Is A automatically connected to C through peering?

choices.A: Yes, resource tags enable transit
choices.C: No, peering only connects storage accounts
choices.D: Yes, every peering chain is transitive

explanations.A: Tags do not establish routing.
explanations.C: Peering connects VNets.

stem: What does DNS primarily do?

choices.A: Grant business permissions
choices.D: Encrypt every packet

explanations.A: Authorization is separate.
explanations.C: DNS supplies name resolution.
explanations.D: Name resolution is not universal encryption.

stem: An office needs encrypted tunnel connectivity to Azure over the internet. Which service fits?

choices.A: ExpressRoute as guaranteed encryption
choices.D: VPN Gateway

explanations.A: Private circuits do not inherently mean all traffic is encrypted.
explanations.B: File shares do not supply a VPN gateway.
explanations.C: Metadata does not create a tunnel.

stem: An organization needs private provider connectivity to Azure. Which offering fits?

choices.A: VPN Gateway over public internet only
choices.D: Azure Table Storage

explanations.A: That is a tunnel across public connectivity.
explanations.B: It supplies private connectivity through providers.
explanations.C: That organizes VM placement.

stem: Which ExpressRoute statement is accurate?

choices.A: Every circuit is simply an internet VPN
choices.B: Private connectivity does not automatically mean universal encryption
choices.D: It creates a private-cloud model for Azure

explanations.A: ExpressRoute uses private provider connectivity.
explanations.C: Private paths still need access controls.
explanations.D: Connectivity does not change Azure ownership.

stem: An empty VNet and subnet have been deployed. What is available?

choices.A: A storage account's private endpoint automatically
choices.B: Addressing space and logical networking infrastructure
choices.D: A running web application automatically

explanations.A: That needs separate service configuration.
explanations.B: The network contains no application instance yet.
explanations.C: No gateway/tunnel was created.

stem: What does a subnet resource ID nested under a VNet show?

choices.A: The subnet is a child network resource
choices.C: The subnet is a management group
choices.D: The subnet is a separate physical region

explanations.A: The ID represents containment within the VNet.
explanations.C: Management groups organize subscriptions.

stem: Which scenario is a natural peering use case?

choices.A: Encrypt a user's password
choices.B: Move archives by shipping a device
choices.D: Connect two Azure VNets with appropriate nonoverlapping design

explanations.A: Authentication handling is separate.
explanations.C: That is information governance.

stem: What must be considered when joining networks?

choices.A: An assumption private addresses authorize every request
choices.C: Address overlap, routing, and security requirements
choices.D: An assumption DNS alone creates routes

explanations.A: Authentication remains separate.
explanations.B: Names do not make ranges routable.
explanations.C: Connectivity needs compatible network design.
explanations.D: Name resolution does not supply a network path.

stem: Two networks use overlapping address ranges. What is the fundamental design concern?

choices.A: Ambiguous or unsupported routing/connectivity
choices.D: Budget notifications disappearing

explanations.A: Overlaps complicate network integration.
explanations.B: Address ranges do not patch operating systems.
explanations.C: Network design does not set storage tiers.
explanations.D: Costs are unrelated to prefix overlap.

stem: A name resolves correctly but traffic still fails. What should be checked next?

choices.A: Only the resource's billing tag
choices.B: Only the DNS spelling again indefinitely
choices.D: Routing, reachability, and traffic rules

explanations.A: Tags do not prove packet reachability.
explanations.C: Tiering does not establish network reachability.
explanations.D: Resolution alone does not prove connectivity.

stem: Which distinction separates peering from VPN Gateway?

choices.A: VPN Gateway is always a file-share cache
choices.C: Peering links VNets; VPN Gateway supports VPN tunnels
choices.D: Peering is user authentication; VPN is budgeting

explanations.A: That describes File Sync, not VPN.
explanations.C: They address different connectivity mechanisms.

stem: Why does a private network still need security controls?

choices.A: Private IPs guarantee every user is trusted
choices.C: Private connectivity does not authorize every workload/user
choices.D: All network rules belong only to visitors

explanations.A: Addressing alone does not establish trust.
explanations.B: Logical networks do not repair applications.
explanations.C: Traffic and identity controls remain necessary.

stem: Which live deployment is included in this lab?

choices.A: A VNet and subnet in the owned group
choices.D: A VM with a public IP

explanations.A: The lifecycle profile deploys these small network resources.
explanations.C: Gateways are discussed but not deployed.
explanations.D: Compute and public IPs are not required.

stem: What makes a public endpoint public?

choices.A: It exists only in private clouds
choices.D: Its address is publicly routable

explanations.A: Public endpoints can occur across models.
explanations.B: Endpoint exposure does not transfer data ownership.
explanations.C: Authentication can still be required.

stem: What does a private endpoint provide?

choices.A: A private IP in a VNet for access to a supported service
choices.D: A new cloud subscription

explanations.A: Private Link integrates service access with private networking.
explanations.C: An endpoint is not data replication.
explanations.D: An endpoint does not create billing boundaries.

stem: A storage account has a private endpoint. Is its public endpoint automatically disabled in every case?

choices.A: No, public access configuration is a separate decision
choices.B: No, private endpoints are always public IPs
choices.D: Yes, all public configuration is deleted

explanations.A: Creating private connectivity does not inherently remove public exposure.
explanations.C: DNS does not delete resources.

stem: Why does private-endpoint DNS matter?

choices.A: DNS eliminates every firewall rule
choices.C: Clients must resolve the service name to the intended private address
choices.D: DNS grants blob data roles

explanations.A: Traffic controls remain relevant.
explanations.C: Correct resolution directs the connection.

stem: A private endpoint resolves to its private IP but a blob request is denied. What could still be missing?

choices.A: A larger VM size
choices.D: A different resource-group name

explanations.A: Compute size does not fix blob access.
explanations.B: Public exposure is not required for data authorization.
explanations.C: Network access does not grant data access.

stem: A public storage endpoint requires Entra authorization. What is true?

choices.A: The account is private cloud
choices.B: Public routing and restricted data access can coexist
choices.D: Public means any visitor can read data

explanations.A: Access settings do not change deployment model.
explanations.B: Endpoint reachability is separate from permission.
explanations.C: Network access does not determine tier.

stem: Which combination supports private service access?

choices.A: Only an availability set
choices.C: Only an account key stored in a public README
choices.D: Private endpoint, appropriate DNS, reachable network, and authorization

explanations.A: VM placement does not create private service access.
explanations.C: Secret exposure does not provide safe network design.

stem: What does creating this lab's VNet alone do to a storage public endpoint?

choices.A: Disable it globally
choices.D: Convert it to SaaS

explanations.A: A separate empty network does not change the account.
explanations.B: Service endpoints/private endpoints need separate configuration.
explanations.C: Network creation does not change blob permissions.
explanations.D: Networking does not select service model.

stem: A client outside the VNet cannot reach a private endpoint. What should be reviewed?

choices.A: An approved path into the network and DNS configuration
choices.B: Whether a tag can replace a VPN
choices.D: Whether anonymous access can bypass routing

explanations.A: Private reachability depends on the client's network path.
explanations.C: Storage tier changes do not resolve routing.

stem: Which statement separates endpoint type from cloud model?

choices.A: A public-cloud service can have private connectivity
choices.B: A private IP always proves private-cloud ownership
choices.C: Endpoint type determines guest OS patching duty
choices.D: Public cloud requires anonymous endpoints

explanations.A: Private endpoint access does not make Azure private cloud.
explanations.B: Public cloud also uses private addresses.
explanations.C: Service model determines that boundary.

stem: A service name resolves to a public IP when private access was intended. What is a sensible first investigation?

choices.A: Changing cost tags
choices.D: Private DNS configuration and resolution path

explanations.A: Metadata does not direct DNS.
explanations.C: Compute capacity does not fix name resolution.
explanations.D: The name may be using public resolution.

stem: Why are endpoint and authorization decisions both necessary?

choices.A: Connectivity determines the path; authorization controls permitted use
choices.B: RBAC automatically creates all network routes
choices.C: A private path replaces all permissions
choices.D: Public routing guarantees data access

explanations.A: They solve different parts of access.
explanations.C: Network isolation is not full authorization.
